questions.question: What is HTML and what is its primary purpose in web development?
questions.answer: HTML structures the content of web pages.
questions.explanation: It labels content such as headings, paragraphs, links, and images so browsers can interpret the document.

questions.question: What does the acronym HTML stand for?
questions.answer: HyperText Markup Language.
questions.explanation: Hypertext connects documents with links; markup describes the structure and meaning of content.

questions.question: What is the basic structure of an HTML document?
questions.answer: A doctype followed by an html element containing head and body.
questions.explanation:
The head holds document metadata, while the body contains the page content. Example: Quiz

Hello

.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration?
questions.answer: It tells the browser to use standards mode.
questions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> is a declaration, not a visible element. It prevents legacy quirks-mode rendering.

questions.question: What is the difference between the <head> and <body> elements?
questions.answer: head contains metadata; body contains page content.
questions.explanation: The title, metadata, and stylesheet links belong in head. Headings, paragraphs, and other displayed content belong in body.

questions.question: What are HTML elements?
questions.answer: Elements are the building blocks of an HTML document.
questions.explanation:
Most have an opening tag, content, and a closing tag, such as

Hello

. Void elements such as do not have closing tags.

questions.question: What are HTML attributes?
questions.answer: Attributes provide additional information or settings for elements.
questions.explanation: They appear in the opening tag, for example href in About.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the title tag?
questions.answer: It gives the document a title.
questions.explanation: Browsers use <title> for the tab label, and bookmarks commonly use it as their default name. It does not create a heading in the page body.

questions.question: What tag is used to create a paragraph in HTML?
questions.answer:
The

tag.
questions.explanation:
A paragraph groups related text:

Welcome to the quiz.

.

questions.question: What are heading tags in HTML?
questions.answer: <h1> through <h6>.
questions.explanation: These represent six heading levels. Choose levels to express the document hierarchy, rather than just to change text size.

questions.question: How do you create a hyperlink in HTML?
questions.answer: Use an <a> element with an href attribute.
questions.explanation: For example, About us creates a link to another page.

questions.question: What attribute specifies the destination of a hyperlink?
questions.answer: The href attribute.
questions.explanation: On an anchor element, href provides the destination URL or a fragment such as #contact for a location in the same page.

questions.question: How do you insert an image in HTML?
questions.answer: Use the element with src and alt attributes.
questions.explanation: For example, . src identifies the image resource and alt supplies a text alternative.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute in an image tag?
questions.answer: It supplies a text alternative for an image.
questions.explanation: Screen readers can announce it, and browsers can use it when an image cannot load. Purely decorative images should usually use alt="".

questions.question: What is the difference between ordered and unordered lists?
questions.answer: Ordered lists use <ol>; unordered lists use <ul>.
questions.explanation: Both contain <li> items. Use an ordered list when sequence matters and an unordered list when it does not.

questions.question: Which tags are used to create a table in HTML?
questions.answer: <table>, <tr>, <th>, and <td>.
questions.explanation: table wraps the table, tr defines a row, th defines a header cell, and td defines a data cell. thead and tbody can group rows.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the form element?
questions.answer: It groups controls for collecting and submitting user input.
questions.explanation: A form can contain inputs, labels, and buttons. Its action and method determine where and how a normal submission is sent.

questions.question: Name three common input types used in HTML forms.
questions.answer: text, email, and password.
questions.explanation: For example, <input type="email"> requests an email address. Input types influence the control’s behavior and built-in validation.

questions.question: What is semantic HTML?
questions.answer: HTML that expresses the meaning of content.
questions.explanation: Using meaningful elements helps browsers, assistive technology, and developers understand a page’s structure.

questions.question: Give three examples of semantic HTML elements.
questions.answer: <header>, <nav>, and <article>.
questions.explanation: header represents introductory content, nav a navigation section, and article a self-contained composition.

questions.question: What is CSS and why is it used?
questions.answer: CSS controls the presentation and layout of web content.
questions.explanation: It lets you style colors, typography, spacing, and layout while keeping those rules separate from HTML structure.

questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.answer: Cascading Style Sheets.
questions.explanation: The cascade is the process used to resolve competing style declarations for an element.

questions.question: What are the three ways to apply CSS to an HTML document?
questions.answer: Inline, internal, and external styles.
questions.explanation: Use a style attribute, a <style> element, or a linked .css file respectively.

questions.question: What is the difference between inline, internal, and external CSS?
questions.answer: Inline styles affect one element; internal styles live in the document; external styles live in a separate file.
questions.explanation: External stylesheets can be shared by multiple pages, making site-wide styling easier to maintain.

questions.question: How do you link an external CSS file to an HTML document?
questions.answer: Use <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> in the head.
questions.explanation: The browser loads the referenced stylesheet and applies its matching rules to the document.

questions.question: What is a CSS selector?
questions.answer: A pattern that identifies which elements a style rule targets.
questions.explanation: For example, .notice selects elements whose class list includes notice.

questions.question: What is the difference between an ID selector and a class selector?
questions.answer: An ID selector uses #; a class selector uses a dot.
questions.explanation: #intro matches id="intro", while .intro matches class="intro". IDs should be unique within a document; classes can be reused. An ID selector has greater specificity than a class selector.

questions.question: How do you select all paragraph elements using CSS?
questions.answer: Use the p type selector.
questions.explanation: For example, p { color: navy; } applies to every paragraph matched by that rule.

questions.question: How do you change the text color of an element using CSS?
questions.answer: Use the color property.
questions.explanation: For example, p { color: blue; } makes paragraph text blue unless another applicable rule overrides it.

questions.question: How do you change the background color of an element?
questions.answer: Use background-color.
questions.explanation: For example, .card { background-color: white; } sets the element’s background color.

questions.question: What property is used to change the font size?
questions.answer: font-size.
questions.explanation: For example, p { font-size: 1.25rem; } sets text size relative to the root element’s font size.

questions.question: What property is used to make text bold?
questions.answer: font-weight.
questions.explanation: For example, strong { font-weight: bold; }. The numeric value 700 commonly corresponds to bold, subject to the font’s available weights.

questions.question: Explain the CSS box model.
questions.answer: Content, padding, border, and margin.
questions.explanation: Padding surrounds the content, the border surrounds the padding, and margin adds outer spacing. With box-sizing: border-box, declared width includes padding and border.

questions.question: What is the difference between margin and padding?
questions.answer: Margin is outside the border; padding is inside it.
questions.explanation: Padding separates content from its border. Margin separates the element’s box from neighboring boxes; vertical margins can sometimes collapse.

questions.question: What is the default position value in CSS?
questions.answer: static.
questions.explanation: A statically positioned element follows normal layout, and top, right, bottom, and left do not offset it.

questions.question: What are the different values of the position property?
questions.answer: static, relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky.
questions.explanation: Relative preserves normal-flow space; absolute leaves normal flow; fixed commonly anchors to the viewport; sticky follows flow then sticks within its scrolling constraints.

questions.question: What is Flexbox in CSS?
questions.answer: A one-dimensional layout system.
questions.explanation: With display: flex, a container arranges children along a main axis and supports alignment, spacing, and wrapping.

questions.question: What is CSS Grid?
questions.answer: A two-dimensional layout system.
questions.explanation: With display: grid, a container places items in rows and columns, making coordinated page and component layouts easier.

questions.question: What is the purpose of media queries?
questions.answer: They conditionally apply CSS based on media features.
questions.explanation: For example, @media (min-width: 768px) { ... } applies its rules when the viewport is at least 768 CSS pixels wide.

questions.question: How can you make a website responsive using CSS?
questions.answer: Use flexible layouts, responsive media, and media queries.
questions.explanation: Flexbox or Grid, relative sizing, and images constrained to their container help content adapt. A viewport meta tag also helps mobile browsers use the intended viewport width.

questions.question: What is Bootstrap?
questions.answer: A frontend toolkit for building responsive websites.
questions.explanation: Bootstrap supplies CSS layouts, utilities, and components, plus JavaScript for interactive components.

questions.question: Who developed Bootstrap?
questions.answer: Mark Otto and Jacob Thornton at Twitter.
questions.explanation: Bootstrap began as an internal Twitter project and was later released as an open-source toolkit.

questions.question: What are the advantages of using Bootstrap?
questions.answer: Reusable components, responsive layouts, and consistent styling.
questions.explanation: Using established patterns reduces repetitive styling work, although accessibility and customization still need attention.

questions.question: How do you include Bootstrap in a project?
questions.answer: Include its CSS and, when needed, its JavaScript.
questions.explanation: You can use a CDN, downloaded files, or a package manager. Interactive components may require the Bootstrap JavaScript bundle; use files from the same version.

questions.question: What is the Bootstrap grid system?
questions.answer: A responsive layout system built from containers, rows, and columns.
questions.explanation: In Bootstrap’s default grid, columns divide a row into portions of a 12-column layout and can change at breakpoints.

questions.question: How many columns are in the Bootstrap grid system?
questions.answer: 12 columns by default.
questions.explanation: A .col-6 spans half the available 12-column row; two such columns fill it. The grid can be customized when compiling Bootstrap.

questions.question: What is the difference between container and container-fluid in Bootstrap?
questions.answer: .container uses responsive maximum widths; .container-fluid stays 100% wide.
questions.explanation: At larger breakpoints, a default container is capped to a set width. Both provide horizontal padding by default.

questions.question: What are Bootstrap utility classes?
questions.answer: Small classes that apply a focused styling rule.
questions.explanation: Examples include .d-flex for display, .text-center for text alignment, and .mt-3 for top margin.

questions.question: What class is used to create a responsive row in Bootstrap?
questions.answer: .row.
questions.explanation: Place column elements inside a .row, usually within a container. The row coordinates column wrapping and gutters.

questions.question: How do you create equal-width columns in Bootstrap?
questions.answer: Use .col on each sibling column.
questions.explanation: For example, two <div class="col"> elements inside a .row share the available width equally when neither has a fixed column size.

questions.question: What Bootstrap class is used to create a button?
questions.answer: .btn.
questions.explanation: Combine the base button class with a variant such as .btn-primary to give it the intended visual treatment.

questions.question: How do you create a primary button in Bootstrap?
questions.answer: Use class="btn btn-primary" on a button.
questions.explanation: For example, <button class="btn btn-primary">Start</button>. btn supplies the base styling and btn-primary supplies the primary variant.

questions.question: What Bootstrap class makes an image responsive?
questions.answer: .img-fluid.
questions.explanation: In Bootstrap 5, this sets max-width: 100% and height: auto so an image can shrink with its parent while preserving its aspect ratio.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Bootstrap navbar component?
questions.answer: It provides a responsive navigation header.
questions.explanation: A navbar can contain branding and links. Collapsible navigation requires suitable markup and Bootstrap’s Collapse JavaScript behavior.

questions.question: How do you create a Bootstrap card?
questions.answer: Wrap content in .card and use .card-body for its main content.
questions.explanation:
For example,
Hello
. Optional classes include .card-title and .card-text.

questions.question: What Bootstrap class is used to create an alert message?
questions.answer: .alert with a variant such as .alert-success.
questions.explanation:
For example,
Saved
. Do not rely on color alone to communicate the message.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Bootstrap's spacing utilities?
questions.answer: They quickly apply margin and padding.
questions.explanation: Their names describe spacing type, side, and size, such as mt-3 for top margin and p-4 for padding on every side.

questions.question: What does the class mt-3 mean in Bootstrap?
questions.answer: Top margin at spacing level 3.
questions.explanation: In Bootstrap 5’s default spacing scale, mt-3 applies margin-top: 1rem. Custom Sass settings can change that value.

questions.question: What does the class p-4 mean in Bootstrap?
questions.answer: Padding on all sides at spacing level 4.
questions.explanation: In Bootstrap 5’s default spacing scale, p-4 applies 1.5rem of padding to every side. Custom spacing settings can change the value.

questions.question: How can Bootstrap help speed up web development?
questions.answer: It provides ready-made layouts, utilities, and components.
questions.explanation: Developers can assemble common interface patterns quickly and customize them instead of writing every style and behavior from scratch.
